A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PEAR research work. Text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and can be matched despite pagination and table-number changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original WMT24 evaluations, MBR decoding experiments, anchor comparisons, loss and antisymmetry ablations, and metric-correlation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds an MT-RANKER comparison, significance rankings, and an additional anchor stress test.

M1.justification: The cross-encoder scorer, scaled utility difference, Huber and antisymmetry losses, and inference modes are retained. Section 3.3 provides more precise projection and feed-forward-head implementation details without establishing an actual change to the method.

E1.justification: Appendix C.1 revises distilled-supervision coverage from five to six additional language pairs, without naming the additional pair. Section 5.4 also extends anchor testing to the substantially lower-quality MSLC outputs. The principal datasets and evaluation languages remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v1 explicitly excludes MT-RANKER from evaluation. v2 adds a dedicated comparison against the 5.7B MT-RANKER-XXL model in Section 5.2 and Table 3. The existing controlled, WMT24, and MBR comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 doubles the reported MQM training pairs from 3M to 6M and distilled pairs from 1M to 2M; these materially revise stated training scale without establishing reruns. New Section 5.2 removes tied MQM pairs and evaluates binary pairwise accuracy on 49,666 English–German, 24,777 English–Spanish, and 34,045 Japanese–Chinese pairs, reporting a macro-average.

E4.justification: The anchor-sensitivity analysis expands from five to six MT anchors, adding MSLC to test robustness to particularly poor anchor translations. The antisymmetry/transitivity analysis, Huber-versus-MSE ablation, and correlation analyses in the appendices are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 2 newly report statistical-significance rankings using the PERM-BOTH hypothesis test; v1 provides only point estimates in these comparisons. This substantially extends statistical assessment of the central results. No additional training runs or seed counts are reported.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports macro pairwise accuracy of 68.9 for PEAR-KD, 68.0 for PEAR, and 65.8 for MT-RANKER-XXL on non-tied pairs. Figure 2 adds MSLC-conditioned ranks, including rank 9 for PEAR-ref, and Tables 1–2 add significance rankings. Previously reported benchmark, MBR, ablation, and correlation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The scoring, aggregation, loss, and inference equations remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the same antisymmetry, additive-transitivity, and normalized-residual definitions. No new or revised proof, theorem, or formal derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about graded pairwise QE, comparative performance, anchoring, metric diversity, and efficient MBR. The added MBR statement in the conclusion repeats a contribution already claimed in v1; the new experiments support existing claims.

C2.justification: The anchor discussion now explicitly interprets robustness to low-quality MSLC outputs and removes v1’s statement that rank shifts are at most one position. The MBR interpretation narrows from a potentially stronger utility than traditional reference-based metrics to an effective utility. The substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 newly specifies projection layer normalization and three hidden feed-forward layers, with widths 512/256/128 for PEAR and 2048/1024/512 for PEAR-XL. Appendix C.1 clarifies that multiple MQM annotations become separate training instances; v1 did not specify their handling. Code and checkpoint access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting layer normalization, significance testing, COMET-22, WMT25 context, GPT-4.1, and comparative human-evaluation platforms. It also replaces the rationale for excluding MT-RANKER with a direct comparison to this closest prior approach. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording, capitalization, and explanatory edits; inserts the MT-RANKER subsection; and adds Ethics Statement and Acknowledgements sections. Limitations becomes unnumbered. The overall narrative and Appendix A–D organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 3, adds significance-rank columns to Tables 1–2, and redraws Figure 2 with MSLC, an expanded rank axis, and revised legend ordering. Existing MBR and ablation tables are renumbered and repositioned. Correlation matrices remain unchanged, with revised captions.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the existing evidence through a direct comparison with the previously excluded closest baseline, significance testing of central comparisons, and a more demanding anchor test. Clearer head and annotation-handling details also improve reproducibility. These are targeted improvements to an already extensive evaluation; revised training counts do not establish reruns or performance gains.
